# html.charset — Page does not declare its character encoding early enough

- **Check ID:** `html.charset`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** HTML Standard
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/html.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/html.charset.md`](../html.charset.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A page does not declare its character encoding within the first 1,024 bytes.

## Why it matters

The browser has to choose a character encoding before it can read the page. If the page does not say which one, the browser guesses, often windows-1252, and any non-ASCII text can appear as garbled characters. A declaration after the first 1,024 bytes is too late for the browser's prescan, so it has the same effect as no declaration.

## What it checks

The page must contain one of the two HTML encoding declarations:

```html
<meta charset="utf-8">
```

```html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8">
```

The element must be serialized completely within the first 1,024 bytes of the file. The check counts bytes, so non-ASCII text before the declaration uses more of the limit than its character count suggests. A leading UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) also satisfies the requirement. Empty values do not count.

The check reads the built file, so it cannot see a `Content-Type` response header from the host. If the host sets the charset header and the file does not declare it, this check still reports the file.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before -->
<head>
  <title>Example</title>
</head>

<!-- after -->
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Example</title>
</head>
```

Put the declaration first in `<head>`, before any other content. In a template or layout, put it at the top of the `<head>` partial. The report suggests an exact insertion when the `<head>` tag is on one line and the file is valid UTF-8. If the file's encoding cannot be confirmed as UTF-8, it gives a manual hint to confirm the actual encoding first: declaring UTF-8 on a page saved in another encoding would relabel the bytes and garble the text. For a late declaration it gives a manual move hint.

## Options

None. Default severity: `error`.

## Standards

- [HTML Standard: character encoding declaration](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-charset)
- [HTML Standard: determining the character encoding](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#determining-the-character-encoding)
